endpoints.name: Agent Weather API
endpoints.description:
AI provider health readings and a combined record for AI agents, each reading with its source and timestamp. `/v1/decide/provider-health` returns one AI provider's status-page reading plus its last 24h in our record; `/v1/agent-weather/current` returns the combined record in one call (AI provider health, x402 payment activity on the XRP Ledger, agent tooling). For XRP Ledger users: x402 merchant readings by XRPL address at `/v1/merchant/{address}`. AI model price readings from the models.dev catalog (MIT): `/v1/models/report` and `/v1/decide/cheapest-model`. Raw readings first; gaps are reported, not filled.

Pay per request with [x402](https://x402.org) v2 (scheme `exact`): RLUSD on the XRP Ledger (`xrpl:0`) or USDC on Base (`eip155:8453`), same price on every paid route. No API key or account.

**Payment flow**
1. Call the paid endpoint without payment and receive **402** with a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header
   (base64 of the same JSON as the body). Each 402 mints a fresh single-use `extra.invoiceId`.
2. Choose an `accepts[]` entry: RLUSD on XRPL (sign an XRPL `Payment` bound to that invoice) or, where offered,
   USDC on Base (sign an EIP-3009 authorization), and retry with the base64 x402 `PaymentPayload` in `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`.
3. The server verifies and settles through the facilitator and re-checks the transaction on-ledger.
   It then returns **200** with the report and a `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header.

Settlement uses the T54 XRPL mainnet facilitator (`https://xrpl-facilitator-mainnet.t54.ai`) for RLUSD and the CDP facilitator for USDC on Base.
Use the `x402-xrpl` client (npm/PyPI). The reference `@x402/xrpl` client currently can't pay through
T54 (https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3527).

If your wallet only signs transactions (for example Privy), pay with USDC on Base; RLUSD on XRPL is for buyers using the `x402-xrpl` client.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Is this address a contract? On Ethereum, Base, Arc or BNB Chain: whether code is deployed, its size, the implementation behind an EIP-1967 or ZeppelinOS proxy, and an EIP-7702 delegation if the address is a wallet that delegates. Pass ?address=&chain=

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Currency exchange rate and conversion, read on chain from Chainlink FX feeds on Ethereum: pass ?from=EUR&to=JPY&amount=100. EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, AUD, CAD, CNY, KRW, SGD, TRY, BRL, NZD, PHP, USD, plus gold (XAU) and silver (XAG). Cross rates come from two USD feeds, and each leg carries its feed address, round and age. endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Sanctions check for a wallet address on any chain: is it on the OFAC SDN list (read from Treasury's official SDN.XML, about 1,060 digital currency addresses: Bitcoin, Tron, Ethereum, USDT, Solana and more), under which entry and programs, with the list's publication date. endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a batch moving native USDC held by the deposit wallet to the bridge (credited as pUSD). Only for USDC already sitting in the deposit wallet — the normal funding path is sending USDC to the bridge deposit addresses from GET /predict/polymarket/wallet/{signer}, which needs no batch. Returns `plan` and `response.actions[0]`, a Batch the chainhilt wallet signs and POSTs to /api/v1/predict/polymarket/wallet/batch/submit.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Construct a prediction-market order; never submits. `account` is the signer EOA; by default the maker is its deposit wallet (signatureType 3). Requires `credentialToken` from /predict/polymarket/credentials. Returns `construction` and a signature action the chainhilt wallet signs and POSTs to /predict/polymarket/orders/submit. Review orderSummary and warnings before signing: `estimatedBuilderFee` (ours) and `estimatedVenueFee` (Polymarket's) are pUSD on top of the principal.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Deterministic prediction-market quote from the live order book: integer micro-unit book walk (buys round principal up, sells round proceeds down). `estimatedVenueFee` is Polymarket's own taker fee at the average price (shares × rate × p × (1 − p), from the market's live fee schedule; null when the venue reports a fee type this API cannot price). Informational only — nothing is reserved.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Deploy the deposit wallet, then add its missing trading approvals, one step per call. Requires the signer's `credentialToken` (401 once revoked). Undeployed: `plan.plan.details.step` is "deploy"; the wallet signs and POSTs the action to /predict/polymarket/wallet/batch/submit, then calls again (202 while pending). Deployed: a Batch of the missing approvals for the same route. 422 "Nothing to onboard" is not charged; GET /predict/polymarket/wallet/{signer} checks for free.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a batch redeeming resolved positions to pUSD; `conditionId` narrows it to one condition. `plan.plan.details.conditions` lists what this batch redeems. Protocol V2 positions go in a batch of their own: when CTF positions are redeemable too, this batch carries those and `plan.plan.details.pendingConditions` lists the V2 conditions for the next prepare. V2 outcomes that pay nothing are skipped. 422 when nothing is redeemable.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Trade and settlement history of a venue account, newest first and cursor-paged: fills (TRADE, with the pUSD that actually moved, fees included), REDEEM, SPLIT/MERGE, CONVERSION and rewards, each with its Polygon transaction hash. Deposits and withdrawals appear only when `type` names them. Filter by `type`, `conditionId`, `side` and an ISO `start`/`end`; to page, pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` with the same filters. The ground truth after an ambiguous submit.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a pUSD withdrawal batch to the bridge routing address. `recipientAddr` defaults to the signer and is echoed in `plan.plan.details.recipient`; check it before signing. 422 when the asset is not on the bridge's list or the amount is under its minimum (2 pUSD for USDC on Base), since the bridge never delivers smaller transfers. On submit, `final` means the pUSD reached the bridge; delivery to the destination chain takes minutes.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Order books for every outcome of a market.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Search prediction markets. `closingAfter`/`closingBefore` bound the venue query; other filters apply after fetching `limit` rows, so a page can be short or empty while `nextCursor` is set: keep paging until it is absent. `sort=closingTime` lists open markets closing soonest; with `closingBefore` it finds short-horizon markets such as the 5-minute crypto up/down slots, which text `query` search never returns.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Held outcome-token positions with PnL and redeemability. Live positions from the venue's public data feed: size, average/current price, cash and realized PnL, and whether each position is redeemable (market resolved). Redemption itself is an on-chain action from the holding wallet; resolved positions redeem to pUSD. `truncated: true` means the upstream page cap was hit and more positions exist.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Return the Hyperliquid noop action the user must sign to mark a nonce as used for safer in-flight cancellation workflows. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Select the best available swap quote and return ordered unsigned transaction actions. Run the returned actions in order: up to two approvals, then the swap.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402

endpoints.description: Prepare a TWAP cancellation for L1 signing. Supply action type twapCancel, asset ID a, and TWAP ID t. Sign and submit unchanged using the returned submitPath. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare an order for L1 signing with the configured lowercase builder and fee in tenths of a basis point. Sign and submit unchanged to the returned submitPath. Missing builder configuration returns 503. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Preview the Hyperliquid cancel-all action the user must sign, optionally scoped to a market. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Preview the Hyperliquid cancel action the user must sign for an open numeric order ID. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a single-order modification by OID or CLOID for L1 signing. Supply the full replacement order. Omit action.a unless true. Sign and submit unchanged using the returned submitPath. See /skills.md for signing rules. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a USDC-only withdrawal to the signing account; other assets return 400. Unified account and portfolio margin accounts must use spot; manual mode may use spot or perp. Arbitrum receives the amount less a fee, and gas comes from the balance left, so the whole balance cannot be withdrawn. Sign the typedData and submit it unchanged to submitPath. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a TWAP order for L1 signing. Supply asset, side, total size, reduce-only, duration of 5 to 10,080 minutes, and randomize. Estimated total value at the current mid must be at least $100 for perps or 100 of the pair's quote token for spot. Builder-deployed perps are not supported. Sign and submit using the returned submitPath. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a user-signed abstraction change: disabled, unifiedAccount, or portfolioMargin. Sign with the account owner's wallet, then submit using the returned submitPath. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Preview a Hyperliquid trade with notional, margin impact, slippage, liquidation estimate, exchange fees, and builder fee. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Audit Hyperliquid open orders for stale, duplicate, conflicting, reduce-only, or unprotected orders. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Return chart-ready Hyperliquid portfolio graph data for account value, PnL, drawdown, deposits, and withdrawals. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare a user-signed sendAsset transfer between users, subaccounts, spot and perp DEXs. Use "" for the default perp DEX and "spot" for spot; perp transfers require the collateral token. Sign with the main wallet and submit unchanged to send-asset/execute (unpaid). Invalid input returns 400; execution may return 422 for rejection or 502 for provider failure. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Detect high leverage, liquidation proximity, concentration, funding drag, and missing stops for a Hyperliquid account. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Produce an agent-ready Hyperliquid portfolio report covering equity, PnL, leverage, margin health, liquidation exposure, and concentration. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Prepare the selected bridge route as ordered unsigned transactions: an exact-amount ERC-20 approval when needed (after an approval to 0 for tokens like Ethereum USDT), then the bridge transaction. Pass the minTargetAmount and maxNativeFee the user accepted; if the fresh quote delivers less or charges more native fee, it returns 409 with quote { adapter, estimatedTargetAmount, minTargetAmount, nativeFee } and no actions. Send the actions before expiresAt.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Set cross or isolated leverage for a perp asset. Supply isCross and positive integer leverage; market limits apply. Sign the L1 preview and submit unchanged to leverage/execute (unpaid). Errors: 400 invalid input, 422 exchange rejection, 502 provider failure. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Compare bridge routes, best first: tokens, estimated and minimum target amounts, fees by token, duration, expiry and the approval each route needs. sourceAmount is exactly what leaves the wallet.

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Resolve an order asset ID from asset (symbol, spot pair, @index, or numeric market index) and sourceDex ("" for default perps, "spot" for spot). Spot IDs are 10000 + spot market index; already formatted IDs are preserved. Token indexes are not market indexes. Unknown or ambiguous assets return 400; provider failures return 502. Use assetId as orders[].a or modify order.a before signing. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Add or remove isolated margin for a perp asset. ntli is a signed integer in millionths of USD: 1000000 adds 1 USD; -1000000 removes 1 USD. isBuy defaults to true. Sign and submit unchanged to isolated-margin/execute (unpaid). Errors: 400 invalid input, 422 rejection, 502 provider failure. Treat spot and perp as one balance only when the account abstraction mode is "unifiedAccount".

endpoints.name: ChainHilt | x402
endpoints.description: Look up a bridge after its transaction was sent, by the adapter that built it and the hash of the bridge transaction on the source chain; layerzero and relay also need the providerRef that bridge/execute returned (0x and 64 hex characters). Poll it every 10 to 15 seconds until the status is filled, refunded or failed; an error answer, such as a 429, is not charged. After a 429, wait the Retry-After seconds.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Look up an Iranian province by its Persian name and return its capital and major cities. Use it to resolve a province in an address, to attach geographic context to a user, or to normalize a location field. Returns the province, its capital and its cities.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Convert a Gregorian (ISO, Western) calendar date to the Jalali, Solar Hijri, Persian or Shamsi calendar used in Iran. Use it to display a date to Iranian users, to schedule work in the Iranian calendar, or to convert a Gregorian deadline into a Jalali date. Returns the Jalali year, month, day and month name.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Normalize Persian (Farsi) text: convert Arabic letter variants (ي, ك) to their Persian forms, unify ZWNJ and spacing, and map Arabic-Indic digits to Persian digits. Use it before indexing, searching or comparing Persian text so that lookalike spellings match. Returns the normalized string.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Transliterate Persian, Dari or Arabic script into Latin letters, optionally as a URL slug. Use it to index Persian text in a Latin-keyword search engine, to build slugs for Persian titles, or to render Persian names in a Latin-only system. Returns the Latin transliteration and, when asked, the slug.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Clean a Persian/Arabic CSV, TSV or text file of up to 5000 rows and get the normalized file back. One flat price for the whole file, not per row: Arabic yeh and kaf become their Persian forms, the ZWNJ half-space is normalised, digits are unified to ASCII, and whitespace and line endings are cleaned. Optionally appends a Latin transliteration column. Send the file base64-encoded in content_b64; the file never leaves this worker's origin beyond the payment check.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Clean a Persian/Arabic CSV, TSV or text file of up to 500 rows and get the normalized file back. One flat price for the whole file, not per row: Arabic yeh and kaf become their Persian forms, the ZWNJ half-space is normalised, digits are unified to ASCII, and whitespace and line endings are cleaned. Optionally appends a Latin transliteration column. Send the file base64-encoded in content_b64; the file never leaves this worker's origin beyond the payment check.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Clean a Persian/Arabic CSV, TSV or text file of up to 50 rows and get the normalized file back. One flat price for the whole file, not per row: Arabic yeh and kaf become their Persian forms, the ZWNJ half-space is normalised, digits are unified to ASCII, and whitespace and line endings are cleaned. Optionally appends a Latin transliteration column. Send the file base64-encoded in content_b64; the file never leaves this worker's origin beyond the payment check.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Convert an amount between Iranian rial and toman, where 1 toman equals 10 rial. Use it when a price is given in one unit and must be shown or billed in the other. Returns the converted amount.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Write an amount of Iranian rial or toman out in Persian words (مبلغ به حروف), as required on Iranian cheques, invoices and contracts. Use it to render a payable amount for a Persian-speaking payer. Returns the amount spelled in Persian words with its unit.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Check whether a given Jalali (Solar Hijri) date is an Iranian public holiday and return the holiday's name if it is. Use it before booking, scheduling or sending a deadline-sensitive action on an Iranian working day. Returns whether it is a holiday and which one.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Return the official Iranian public holidays for a Jalali (Solar Hijri) year, with each holiday's Gregorian date and name. Use it to plan delivery or support schedules around Iranian holidays, or to flag non-working days. Returns the holiday list.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: List all 31 Iranian provinces with their capitals and major cities. Use it to populate a province dropdown, to build a location picker, or to validate a region name. Returns every province.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Write an integer out in Persian words (عدد به حروف), for example 1234 as هزار و دویست و سی و چهار. Use it for Persian invoices, cheque amounts, legal and official forms, and display. Returns the number spelled in Persian words.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Look up an Iranian city by its Persian name and return the province it belongs to. Use it to resolve a city in an address or to group a location by region. Returns the city and its province.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate and normalize an Iranian landline number with its area code (021 for Tehran and so on) and resolve that area code to a city. Use it to verify a fixed-line contact or to route a support request to the right region. Returns validity, the normalized number, the area code and the city.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate an Iranian company national ID (شناسه ملی اشخاص حقوقی, the 11-digit legal-entity identifier) by recomputing its check digit. Use it when onboarding a business customer or validating an Iranian legal entity. Returns validity and the parsed digits.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate an Iranian postal code (کد پستی, the 10-digit code) by recomputing its check digit. Use it before using a postal code for delivery or address validation. Returns validity, the normalized code and its province.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate an Iranian economic code (کد اقتصادی, the 12-digit taxpayer identifier) by recomputing its check digit. Use it when validating the tax identifier on an Iranian invoice or a supplier record. Returns validity and the parsed digits.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Convert a Jalali (Solar Hijri, Persian, Shamsi) calendar date to the Gregorian calendar. Use it to turn a date written in the Iranian calendar back into an ISO 8601 date, to check whether a Jalali date is today, or to compare an Iranian deadline with a Western one. Returns the Gregorian year, month, day and weekday.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate an Iranian bank card number, called a PAN (کارت بانکی), with the Luhn check digit, and return the issuing bank. Use it before charging a card or accepting card details from a customer. Returns validity, the masked number and the bank name.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Remove Unicode bidi control characters and repair the spacing around right-to-left punctuation. Use it to clean Persian or Arabic text that renders in the wrong order or shows stray markers. Returns the cleaned string.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Strip HTML tags and decode HTML entities out of a string, leaving the readable text behind. Use it to clean web pages or scraped content before feeding it to an agent or an index. Returns the plain text.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Measure the similarity of two Persian strings as a trigram Jaccard score from 0 to 1. Use it to detect near-duplicate Persian text, deduplicate a corpus, or rank one Persian string against another. Returns the similarity score.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Split Persian text into sentences, handling the Persian question mark ؟, the exclamation mark, ellipsis … and abbreviation boundaries. Use it to chunk Persian text for summarization, translation or per-sentence processing. Returns the list of sentences.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Extract the frequent keywords from Persian text, filtering Persian and English stopwords and ranking by frequency. Use it to build a search index, an automatic tag list, or a topic summary for a Persian document. Returns the ranked keywords.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate and normalize an Iranian mobile phone number, checking the operator prefix (MCI, Irancell, Rightel, Shatel) and the national format 09xxxxxxxxx. Use it to verify a phone number on a sign-up form or before sending an SMS. Returns validity, the normalized number and the operator.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate an Iranian IBAN, called Sheba (شبا), with the ISO 13616 mod-97 check, and return the bank code. Use it before sending or crediting an Iranian bank transfer. Returns validity, the normalized IBAN and the bank identifier.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Validate an Iranian national ID (کد ملی, code melli) by recomputing its check digit. Use it before accepting an identity number from a form, a customer, or an API payload. Returns whether the number is valid, and the parsed digits.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Measure Persian text: character count, word count, line count and the number of ZWNJ half-space characters. Use it to size a Persian document, enforce a length limit, or report text statistics for Persian content. Returns a stats object.

endpoints.name: farsi-tools
endpoints.description: Convert the digits inside a string between Persian (۰-۹), Arabic-Indic (٠-٩) and ASCII (0-9) numeral systems, leaving the rest of the text untouched. Use it to make Persian text machine-readable or to render an ASCII number in Persian script. Returns the converted string.

endpoints.name: Laevitas API V2
endpoints.description:
Professional market data API for crypto derivatives, spot markets, prediction markets, Hyperliquid HyperCore data, proprietary volatility surfaces, and analytics.

## Authentication

Use an API key for authenticated REST requests:

```http
X-API-Key: your-api-key-here
```

Data and history endpoints also accept x402 without an API key: 1, 5 or 10 credits ($0.001 each) for data up to 1 year, 1–3 years or older.

**Subscriptions with USDC:** Premium and Enterprise can be purchased on Base or Solana for a month, a quarter, six months or a year. Access is prepaid, with no automatic renewal. [Buy a subscription](https://v3.laevitas.ch/profile/subscription/wallet) or read the [USDC subscription guide](/x402#subscriptions).

The subscription belongs to your signed-in Laevitas account; wallet sign-in does not require an email. Enterprise users generate an API key in V3 after activation. Plan and billing-period limits still apply. Subscription purchases are separate from API credit bundles.

For Claude MCP, add `https://apiv2.laevitas.ch/api/v1/mcp`, select **Sign in now → Register automatically**
with no custom headers, and authorize with your API key on the Laevitas page.
Do not enter a client ID or secret manually. All OAuth clients require PKCE S256.
Connection guide: [MCP setup](/mcp). CIMD / published client identity is not supported.

| Resource | Path |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAPI JSON | `GET /openapi.json` |
| x402 discovery | `GET /.well-known/x402` |
| Changelog | `GET /api/v1/changelog` |
| WebSocket docs | `GET /websocket` |

## REST Surfaces

| Surface | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Instruments | Cross-market contract reference data |
| Futures | OHLCVT, trades, tickers, orderbook, liquidations, carry |
| Perpetuals | OHLCVT, trades, funding, open interest, orderbook, liquidations |
| Options | OHLCVT, trades, Greeks, volatility, flow, dealer GEX |
| Options Backtests | Strategy templates, asynchronous submission, status, combined results, cancellation |
| Vol Surface | Proprietary surface snapshots, slices, strikes, term structure, risk |
| Spot | OHLCVT, ticker, trades, volume, L2 orderbook, snapshots |
| Predictions | Polymarket instruments, categories, trades, ticker history |
| Hyperliquid - HyperCore | Node-derived fills, liquidations, positions, funding, TWAPs, resting orders, L2 books |
| Analytics | Realized volatility and derived metrics |

## Pagination

Backtests are asynchronous jobs, not paginated market-data queries. Start with
`GET /api/v1/options/backtests/strategies`, submit with `POST /api/v1/options/backtests`,
then poll `/{id}` and retrieve `/{id}/result`. These responses have no data/meta wrapper.

Paginated endpoints return the cursor at `meta.next_cursor`. Pass that value back as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page.

## WebSocket Streaming

Real-time streams are documented at `/websocket`.

| Data | Channel pattern |
| --- | --- |
| Trades | `trades.{market}.{exchange}.{instrument}` |
| OHLC ticker | `ohlc.ticker.{market}.{exchange}.{instrument}.{timeframe}` |
| OHLCVT | `ohlc.vt.{market}.{exchange}.{instrument}.{timeframe}` |

Variables: `market` is one of `perpetuals`, `futures`, `options`, or `spot`; `timeframe` is one of `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `1h`, `4h`, or `1d`.

## Quick Start

```bash
curl "https://apiv2.laevitas.ch/api/v1/futures/ohlcvt?exchange=deribit&instrument_name=BTC-PERPETUAL" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-api-key-here"
```

endpoints.description: Execute up to three registered data/utility operations in one fixed $0.010 USDC purchase. No recursive bundles or arbitrary commands.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Inspect a caller-supplied OpenAPI document and enumerate operations. No endpoints are called and no external $refs are fetched.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Convert GET operations in a caller-supplied OpenAPI document to OpenAI function metadata; no remote execution or credentials are provided.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search a build-time snapshot of APIs.guru OpenAPI catalogue metadata. References are not executable integrations and may need auth/paid plans.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search the official MCP Registry metadata. Listing a server does not grant its credentials or execute its tools.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: List currency codes/names supported by the Frankfurter reference-rate API. Does not provide live trading quotes.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read public current ISS orbit-position estimates, speed and altitude. Not flight-safety or navigation data.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read only metadata and links from one public HTTPS page; no login, CAPTCHA or access-control bypass, and no full article resale.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Extract bounded JSON-LD records from caller-supplied HTML. Data is untrusted and does not execute code or resolve external references.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Extract title, metadata and links from caller-supplied HTML, without fetching resources or running JavaScript.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Convert caller-supplied HTML to bounded Markdown using a parser; strips scripts/styles and unsafe link protocols. Not a browser or CAPTCHA bypass.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read ECB reference exchange rates over a maximum 31-day period, not intraday/trading prices.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Get recent World Bank observations for a country and indicator. Historical statistics, not real-time values or a forecast.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Look up Nager.Date public-holiday dates for a supported country/year. Regional rules may vary; no legal guarantee.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Get recent M2.5+ USGS earthquake feed records, filtered by a supplied minimum magnitude. Not an emergency notification service.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read active US National Weather Service alerts for a US state/area. Not a substitute for official emergency channels.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search the Research Organization Registry for institutions and their identifiers. Returns public CC0 metadata.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Get World Bank country metadata: capital, income group, region and geographic reference coordinates.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Look up biomedical citation metadata by record ID and source; does not retrieve the article text.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search Crossref DOI metadata. Returns citation facts and links, not article full text or copyrighted abstracts.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search biomedical publication metadata in Europe PMC. Research information, not diagnosis or treatment advice.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Retrieve one OpenAlex work by W identifier; metadata only.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: List public Docker Hub image tags and architecture/digest metadata. No image is pulled or run.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search OpenAlex scholarly metadata through its anonymous public API. Free anonymous quotas may limit availability.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Retrieve bibliographic metadata for a DOI, not the paper itself.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read latest release metadata from the public Go module proxy. Does not retrieve or execute source code.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read RubyGems public package metadata, runtime dependencies and latest version; does not install the gem.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Get available versions of a public NuGet package from Microsoft's flat-container API.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Look up a Rust crate on crates.io, including latest version, download counts and repository link.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: List recent Rust crate versions, licenses and yanked flags. Does not install code.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Search public GitHub repositories by query and return compact metadata. Anonymous GitHub search quotas apply.

endpoints.description: Get metadata and downloadable artifact hashes for an explicit PyPI release, without installing or redistributing the artifacts.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Get declared runtime/peer/optional dependencies from one npm package release; no package is installed or executed.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Get the npm registry's recorded package download count for the last week or month, not unique users.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read public repository license identification without redistributing the complete license file or source code.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read public GitHub repository metadata, license identifier, stars, open issue count and archive status.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read DNS-over-HTTPS authenticated-data flags for a hostname. Resolver validation is not an independent DNSSEC audit.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: List tag names and commit SHAs of a public GitHub repository.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Read the latest published release of a public GitHub repository, including artifact metadata; no downloads are executed.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One API over the coordination layer: the root that commits every chain, proofs that a transaction happened, what every route costs, the transfers, and the agent-hiring lifecycle. Most operations are public reads. Writes say who may make them in `security` (RelayerKey = X-API-Key, OperatorToken = x-operator-token) and in x-taifoon-auth.rule; nothing here signs or sends a transaction for you. A 2xx JSON object answered to a caller that sent no key also carries `get_key` (and the headers x-taifoon-get-key and Link rel=free-key): how to get a free key in one call; proofs, evidence packs, cards and this document are left as written. Lineage language: a sale walks offer in → classify → listed → hired → delivered → graded → settled → legs written → accrued → split → PAID → recorded; a venue adapter has offer.in · offer.out · job.in · job.out; the seller of record pays on by forward · share · period · markup; a leg is Owed → Reserved → Sent | Held | Refunded; a hop reads OK · HELD · MISSING · BROKEN. On the wire the hop ids are the event field step and the metric label stage; a wire name is never renamed.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Enlist an expert of the tenant's product: { expert key:<24hex>, payee (an address, or the expert's key ref until it claims one), chains, share_bps ≤ 7000, cap per period, classes } → a nomination sma.nomination.v1 in state proposed; the expert POSTs { id, accept: true } to accept; the admin POSTs { id, revoke: true } to revoke.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Close the loop on a case: answer it (words, by an expert, an agent or a member), grade it (Jev, the buyer or the admin), or tune a loop of the tenant inside its bounds (admin only). A graded answer becomes a fix node and a fixed_by edge; the provider leg goes to the answerer's nominated payee; the meter line is written.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The product's knowledge graph as the helpdesk holds it (?product=<id>, ?scope=public|product|tenant, ?weakest=1 for the ranked unknowns): nodes { id, kind, scope, label, confidence, asked, learned_from }, edges { from, to, kind, weight }, open { category, license, weights, source }.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Show Me Around ++ the helpdesk (_SMA_HELPDESK_v1_, lang/cue/sma-helpdesk.cue): one question about one product → a case. The product's graph answers first (free, measured); an unknown is routed to a nominated expert, the tenant's agent or a person; every answer is graded before it is settled as one sma.case line (0.10 USDC above the free allowance of 20 a day per key; legs provider 70 · graders 20 · ecosystem 10); the trail is sealed under the tenant's topic helpdesk.<name>, read by nobody but th

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Chain Desk's state per chain in the Prometheus text format (_DESK_METRICS_v1_), to scrape into an exchange's own monitoring; ?format=json for JSON.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: State proof of an account at a final block (_DESK_PROOFS_v1_): its nonce and native balance, and one ERC-20 balance by its slot; an address with no account is proven absent.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Completeness proof over final blocks (_DESK_PROOFS_v1_): every ERC-20 transfer to (in) or from (out) an address in a range, and a proof there is no other; NONE proves absence.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Membership proof of one EVM transaction (_DESK_PROOFS_v1_): it is in a final block under the superroot, who signed it, and exactly which ERC-20 transfers it moved; the bundle verifies offline.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The desk_deposits lane of /v1/stream on its own connection (the same events, named as before). Server-sent events of the deposits to watched addresses: each transfer once per level it reaches (seen, confirmed, final), resumable by Last-Event-ID.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The deposit lambda registry: the built-in lambdas (evm, tron, substrate) and the third-party manifests (data only), each with its family, chains, finality, hash and whether a reader exists.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer

endpoints.description: The Chain Desk's chains (_DESK_API_v1_): every chain the desk serves with its family (evm, tron, substrate), CAIP-2 id, finality rule, sources and health, and what a desk should do now.

endpoints.description: Record a batch-judge outcome for the coordination layer (relayer key required).

endpoints.description: The evidence Jev reads about one job the observatory keys — an ERC-8183 / memo-ACP job, an extra deployment’s job, or an assurance-hook job by its 32-byte id (the layer’s hook or Moonbeam ACP’s): task, price, parties, the timeline with the deadline, how it ended, the seller’s record and this buyer’s history with this seller, plus what is not known.

endpoints.description: The evidence pack for one Olas Mech marketplace request on Base — the public prompt, tool, mech, fee and response.

endpoints.description: HashProof, an ERC-8004 agent on Celo, for discovery: the ERC-8004 agents that publish its MCP endpoint, and credentials in its CredentialRegistry on Celo, read on chain in one batch (_CELO_8004_LANE_v1_).

endpoints.description: The A2A Registry (a2aregistry.org) for discovery: agents with the URL their card publishes, the A2A dialect, whether it is free to call, the registry’s own health checks, a live card probe, and ERC-8004 cross-links (_A2A_REGISTRY_v1_).

endpoints.description: Coinbase AgentKit workers registered with the layer: the release, its action providers, the actions each serves, a live probe (_AGENTKIT_LANE_v1_).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The /v1/metrics headline per UTC day for charts, Taifoon’s own vs customers, oldest first (_COORD_METRICS_v1_).

endpoints.description: The gateway counters, the feed /v1/metrics reads for calls through the gateway: in total, per resource, per JSON-RPC method, per ending state and per day (off-chain).

endpoints.description: The official MCP registry for discovery: servers with the endpoint they published, whether it is free to call, a live probe, and ERC-8004 cross-links (_MCP_REGISTRY_v1_).

endpoints.description: The x402 Bazaar for discovery: resources paid through the CDP facilitator, each a payable row with its prices and readiness; nothing is paid (_X402_BAZAAR_v1_).

endpoints.description: The resale wall of one class, probed with GET: the x402 challenge (PAYMENT-REQUIRED) without a body, or the answer with the input as query parameters and a payment (_X402_GET_WALL_v1_).

endpoints.description: One Fetch.ai agent as a hirer needs it: its own Almanac record and the request models its protocols declare.

endpoints.description: Fetch.ai Agentverse agents from its own public search: address, hosting type, protocols, interactions (_AGENTVERSE_LANE_v1_).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Olas Mech marketplace on every chain it runs on (Gnosis, Base, Polygon, OP Mainnet, Robinhood Chain) in one read: every mech with its chain, how it is paid, its card with each tool’s input/output schema, which tools actually answer, and its ERC-8004 agent id.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Virtuals sellers on chain and in Virtuals’ own agent registries, joined by wallet: the memo-ACP sellers on Base and the ACP v3 sellers on Base, Arc and Robinhood, each with its ERC-8004 agent id, ACP v2 agent id, offerings and metrics, and how a buyer outside Virtuals hires one with Taifoon as the evaluator.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The result document a mech delivery points at, byte for byte: keccak256 of the body equals the resultHash on chain.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One coordination mech request: its state, the task, every event with its transaction, the result pointer, and how to refund it when it is refundable.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every coordination mech request, newest first, folded from its events on chain.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The task document and the unsigned approve + request calls for a coordination mech request. Nothing signs here.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The coordination layer as a mech: post a request on chain (a grade, a V5 proof, an agent readiness or match), the layer’s worker delivers the result hash + URI on chain.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Calls, payers and revenue of the two paid trading routes (market/candles, trading/record), outside vs Taifoon’s own by the paying wallet.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Record a Grid hire and, when both sides have wallets, plan its settlement on the assurance hook.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every provider on the Grid, their resources and measured GRID.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Where the Grid is short: chains and kinds ranked by demand, with the bootstrap budget and the settlement rule.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: My GRID: a wallet’s measured ledger, what was settled on Taifoon mainnet, what is pending, and its balance.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Resource pools: several operators’ resources working as one, with the pool’s fee (at most 30%, locked at join).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What the Grid earns: the live rate per kind, and the attribution of revenue to every node behind Taifoon (the one provider at every outlet).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The work coord placed on a node: outlet jobs and Taifoon buyers' work arrive here, never through the contributor's own outlet accounts.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: A taifoon-node's signed heartbeat, every 5 minutes: what the box offers now (capacity per kind), its payout election, and the usage receipts of the work it ran.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Bring a resource to the Grid in one request: the oracle probes it every hour and pays GRID for measured work.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The jobs a grader is needed for: paid and delivered with no ruling, paid and delivered then rejected, funded and past the deadline with no ending — ranked by what is at stake, each with how complete its evidence is.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Many jobs’ ERC-8183 trails in one call, prepared: a finished job’s trail is read once and kept.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every place this layer uses TypeSafe’s Jev, driven through the API and landed on the devnet as its own transaction.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: score(job): grade any job of the lambda catalogue under RUBRIC_v2 — an agent job on an ERC-8183 venue reads its evidence pack; a cross-chain order or a stream-service order step is graded on its observed stages and their proof under the superroot.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Ask for your own Jev seat, or drop it: { action: create | revoke }. The seat is certified within a minute; its key never leaves the Jev unit’s memory.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The layer’s own contract actions on the devnet — hook funds/submits/completes, verdicts, x402 captures, stamps, judge decisions, ERC-8004 feedback — read as genome lines, each a log with its transaction.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Taifoon as the evaluator of a job: the JudgeAdapter a buyer names as evaluator and the V4 hook per network (Base, Arbitrum One, Arc, Robinhood Chain, Monad, the devnet), the fee rule the hook escrows, the rubric hash, and the two-line recipe for a seller and for a buyer.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every live Taifoon contract on every chain, read into genome observations: V4 hooks, fee-forwarding adapters, pools, assurance markets and outcome sources, the Jev arbiter and logs, the V5 verifier set, CCTP routers, the ICP light client (all from the address registry), the Solana devnet programs and the x402 settlements the settle watcher proved.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One recorded Jev answer: the canonical body, its recomputed digest, and the JevAnswered transaction.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Record Jev answers the layer did not fetch (an n8n TypeSafe node, the registry, a runner): stored, digested and, when `record` names a network, anchored on its JevAnswerLog.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every answer Jev gave this layer — each question, value, the full distribution, model, latency and the credential that paid — recorded as a jev.answer.v1 body with its digest on the devnet JevAnswerLog.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Alias of POST /v1/judge/decisions/:id/record with network "base": put an already-recorded judge decision and its answer record on Base (JevDecisionLog + JevAnswerLog, chain 8453), signed by the recorder 0xe9F0E71e7Fc66864126C0aE5588a7858b25dE51D, the only address JevAnswerLog trusts on Base.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Put an already-recorded judge decision and its answer record on one more network: { network } is the name or chain id of a live network, or a list (GET /v1/judge/record/networks). Charged once per decision and network: a network already paid for, queued or recorded is queued again at no charge.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Where a Jev grade may be recorded on chain, and what a record costs there now: one row per network with its chain id, the two logs (JevAnswerLog, JevDecisionLog), whether it is live, and the price of one recorded grade in USDC and in bought grades. The Taifoon devnet is the only free one.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One recorded judge decision with its anchors resolved and the calldata a reader recomputes.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every decision the judge made for this layer — pad picks, skill rankings, assembles, grades, study batteries — each with a recomputable digest and its transaction on the devnet JevDecisionLog.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Venice's name for the System One API (POST /api/v1/decisions there): the same handler as POST /v1/systemone, so a client written for either host reaches coord by changing only its base URL.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The System One standard on coord: the same request and answer TypeSafe and Venice serve (POST /v1/systemone), one host for every provider in lang/cue/systemone.cue. The model may be spelled as any provider spells it (jev-1.13.0, jev-1-13-0, typesafe-jev, jev-latest); coord sends the chosen provider's spelling.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The economy per network (Base, Arbitrum, Arc, Robinhood, Monad, Solana; the devnet apart as test money): callers whose job there was graded (Taifoon’s own apart), grades (house or callers, paid, recorded on Base or the devnet), hires the layer settled, the evaluator fee earned and coverage pools opened.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The case catalogue: every settled job whose ending or grade somebody decided — the Jev arbiter’s rulings, the endings code or Jev decided, the Jev sampler’s grades — on every chain (the devnet V4 hooks, Base, Arbitrum, Monad x402, Solana devnet), newest first, each told in three plain lines: case (task, delivery and its correctness as code or Jev established it), outcome (who got what), decided (code / Jev / Jev arbiter and the rubric).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Jev sampler: every Nth settled job per chain × lane × class graded by Jev under RUBRIC_v2 on the facts code establishes, recorded through the decision ledger, and compared with the code grader’s verdict. POST { regrade: [ids] } with x-operator-token grades sampled jobs again under RUBRIC_v2 as new decisions; the superseded grade stays in the row’s history[].

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Ask Jev for the grade of an open-class demand (a class with no code check).

endpoints.description: Ask Jev for the grade a step of a run is waiting for.

endpoints.description: One run of a flow, moved to its next step by the read.

endpoints.description: The ledger of a flow: each ended run as use or practice, its credits and the legs of its fee.

endpoints.description: The unfinished edges of a flow.

endpoints.description: The runs of flows, newest first.

endpoints.description: One flow listed as an agent, with its flow and record.

endpoints.description: Try a designed flow: keep it as the caller’s draft (not listed, never credited) and run it once on the devnet direct lane.

endpoints.description: Ask the studio agent: it reads, measures and debugs through the layer’s own operations (filtered by your role) and proposes any change as a taifoon command for you to run. The same agent as taifoon ask / taifoon studio.

endpoints.description: Publish a flow: ordered steps, each a class with its input from the need or an earlier step’s output, an optional seller, how it is graded and how it settles.

endpoints.description: Contribute to the coordination layer: a transitions file, a λ machine, a decoder, a schema, a protocol manifest, a module, or an agent.

endpoints.description: GRID given and consumed, as numbers.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Claim a wallet’s helper credit, once.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What a helper of I HELP ONBOARD has earned.

endpoints.description: The season’s earners, outside earners only.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The GRID leaderboard and stats: who gives to the Grid and who uses it, per category, today, this season and all time.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One wallet’s GRID, given and consumed (My GRID).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: A grader’s quality score for a live definition or module: commit, then reveal.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Credit a closed season’s payout to the GRID ledger.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The season’s usage ledger: every settled, graded job and the credits it gave down what it used.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: How GRID is earned and what consuming the layer costs in it.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Spend settled GRID on grades.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Claim a relayer key for a paid transaction on Base — one key per transaction, only by the wallet that paid.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Credit a paid transaction to your identity, once.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Buy blocks of three grades: the unsigned USDC transfer to sign (dUSDC on the devnet today).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The stream’s lanes as one JSON — a first paint in one call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every workflow of the layer on one server-sent event stream: the root every 10 s, the judge’s decisions, the devnet contract actions, the job market, the pools, the onboarding flows, your own judge standing, and the Chain Desk's finality and deposits (_DESK_LANES_v1_).

endpoints.description: The stages of a hire, defined once in the whitepaper’s words and shared with every component (console, MCP, n8n, SDK).

endpoints.description: One recorded settlement, by job id (or the old runner’s <at>-<kind> id).

endpoints.description: One operator step by job id, or one operator decision by its id (opdec-<16 hex>).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The operator steps: held needs_review jobs waiting for, or ended by, an operator’s recorded decision — Jev’s decision and the operator’s side by side.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The settlement watcher: settle rows discovered from the chain with nobody posting — every live V4 line (Base, Arbitrum, the devnet lines) and every x402 network the layer’s payers paid on (Monad, Base), one cursor per lane.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Record a V4 job that ended with nobody deciding: the devnet keeper’s claimAutoComplete, finalizeReject or settleStaleDispute, proven from the chain, on the job’s settle row with the machine’s transition id.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The evaluator leg: the job’s evaluator ends a job on chain from the recorded decision — the verdict a grade decided (complete | reject), or, on a job held on needs_review, the operator’s own recorded decision — one unsigned JudgeAdapter.postVerdict, never a second judge call. Jev’s answer is never replaced.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The unsigned settlement of one paid call — a judge call, a call to another agent, or a grid resource call — on the coordination layer.

endpoints.description: Run the DET-vs-Jev study on calibrated jobs from the whole harvest and record it.

endpoints.description: Report a review: the delivery you re-derived from chain through your own RPC.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Jev pad: every field of a phase as a typed multiple-choice question over live data, answered by ONE calibrated call.

endpoints.description: Read an assembled hire path (the shareable record).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One helper action on one agent, credited to the helper: probe it now, count a copied message to its operator, confirm a listing, confirm a first offer.

Read-only: nothing is registered, minted, probed or paid.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The onboarding graph (_ONBOARD_GRAPH_v1_, coord lang/cue/onboard-graph.cue): every reference point an agent is checked on, the gate it answers to, the check that proves the gate, the fix and who clears it, the op that proves it, the tour step that walks it, the classes, the onboard flow and the hops of a sale, derived from the language. Read-only.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Check an agent against the one agent spec (_AGENT_SPEC_v1_, coord lang/cue/agent-spec.cue): every reference point OK, FIX or MISSING with the fix words and who fixes it, the totals per gate (H1–H4 and the almost-hireable checks) and whether it is ready to be listed. Read-only: nothing is registered, minted or probed.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The agents that are almost hireable, for anyone to help over the line: the first check of the one hireable definition each fails, or hireable but not listed, or listed with no first offer.

endpoints.description: The first onboarding batch: the agents that answered on the wire, in their own protocol.

endpoints.description: Rebuild the onboarding flows from the live harvest, jobs feed and registry (what the delivery loop calls).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
